We need to determine number of methyl (CH3) groups in the sample's molecule. We need the molecule structure. We have no SMILES given. We can retrieve NMR spectra? Probably we need to infer from NMR data. But we have no data yet. We can request proton NMR spectra for a given SMILES, but we don't have SMILES. We could request carbon NMR spectra for sample at hand, but we don't know sample. Maybe there is a default sample? The tool carbon_nmr_spectra takes no args, returns spectra for sample at hand. Similarly hsqc. So we can get NMR data and deduce number of methyl groups.

Methyl groups appear as singlet (or doublet if adjacent to CH) around 0.9 ppm for aliphatic. In 13C, methyl carbon around 10-30 ppm.

We can request carbon NMR spectra.
